## What this dashboard shows

- This dashboard demonstrates how a single ontology spine ensures that finance KPIs (EBITDA and debtor days/DSO) are defined consistently across all legal entities and ERP systems, so the CFO, board, and agents all use the same numbers.
- EBITDA is calculated using 1 formula owned by the Group CFO, which maps to 4 group accounts and 175 local accounts across 5 ERPs, with none left unmapped.
- DSO (debtor days) is defined as Trade receivables / trailing 3-month revenue x 91, reading from 38 local accounts; the agent passed 20/21 test questions in its last evaluation.

## What to report

- Group-wide EBITDA definition is standardized: Revenue - cost of sales - operating expenses, using 4 group accounts (G4000, G5000, G5100, G6000) consistently across all entities and ERPs (SAP S/4HANA (A) and (B), Dynamics 365, Tally Prime, Oracle EBS).
- 175 local accounts across 5 ERPs are fully mapped to the EBITDA group accounts with zero unmapped accounts, ensuring consistent consolidation.
- Newly acquired companies can report on group definitions as soon as their ledger is mapped; Kawasaki Precision Machinery's 9 Tally Prime ledgers already align to EBITDA accounts without KPI definition changes.
- DSO is governed with a single definition (synonym "debtor days") using G1200 and G4000; Consumer Care International reported 207 days as of 2026-07.

## Watch out for

- The data combines real SAP BDC data with simulated ERP data (Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, Tally Prime ledgers); KPI definitions and synonyms are curated for demo purposes, not production.
- The agent's 20/21 pass rate on test questions means 1 failure remains—CFO should ask: which test case failed and what is the remediation plan?
- Kawasaki Precision Machinery books using ledger names rather than account numbers in Tally Prime—confirm that naming-convention governance is robust enough to prevent mapping drift during month-end close.
- Verify that the "none left unmapped" claim for the 175 local accounts holds after the next acquisition or ERP upgrade, and confirm the process for maintaining mapping rules at scale.
